author: agent
text:
DEFECT found in the 0.54.0 launch acceptance, 2026-08-16: an AMBIGUOUS bare name is reported as "no entity matches '<name>'", which is factually false and sends the caller down the wrong path - they conclude the entity is unmapped and fall back to grep, when in fact the map knows several and only needs one disambiguated.

Measured twice. In itsdangerous, five entities end in .get_signature (Signer, SigningAlgorithm, NoneAlgorithm, HMACAlgorithm, and a test class) and `memway show <repo> get_signature` answers "no entity matches 'get_signature'". In memway itself, three entities are named .save and `memway show . save` answers "no entity matches 'save'". The qualified form resolves instantly in both cases.

This is the agent-facing path: a fresh agent briefs itself with a bare name lifted from a diff or a traceback, and a false negative here is the difference between using the map and abandoning it. It also undercuts the actionable-errors work (finding #21), which added hybrid refs and error text that names what to do next - that improvement evidently does not cover the ambiguous case.

Wanted: "'get_signature' is ambiguous - 5 entities match:" followed by the qualnames, exactly as the resolver already knows them, and a nonzero exit. The candidates are in hand at the moment of failure; only the message is wrong.

author: cli
text: Re-read at 0.56.0 - and this is the confirm that was written expecting to stale here, which it now has. The suffix index is keyed by refs.short_of on BOTH sides, so a bare reference reaches a disambiguated registration: 'memway show gson upperCaseFirstLetter' answers instead of claiming no entity matches. Ambiguity is broken by arity when the reference declares one, and only then - a bare name still falls through to the production-over-test rule rather than being silently narrowed to whichever overload happened to match. The O(1) claim is unaffected; the key changed, not the structure.
